concept_name: The Law of Karma and Retribution
english_name: Karma Law of Cause and Effect
definition: The Journey to the West world follows the karmic law 'good is rewarded with good, evil with evil, and as is the cause so is the fruit.' The types of cause and effect fall into ten categories: punishment for disobedience / retribution in kind / benevolent transformation / atonement / cultivation through reincarnation / retribution for lust / punishment for negligence / predestined marriage / tribulation testing / reform
core_principle: Karma outweighs Heaven's decree — the Jade Emperor's edict can be overturned by karma (e.g., the Jing River Dragon King's execution was karma's due); karma outweighs the registers (the register can be changed but karma cannot be escaped)

cases.case_name: The Jing River Dragon King Defies and Is Executed
cases.cause: Bet with Yuan Shoucheng, violated the Jade Emperor's edict, and altered the rain timing and amount
cases.effect: Wei Zheng executed him in a dream at the Dragon-Slaying Terrace; his head fell onto a Chang'an street and his ghost haunted Li Shimin, causing his Underworld tour
cases.karma_principle: Heaven's decree can change, karma cannot be escaped; disobedience brings immediate retribution

cases.case_name: The King of Wuji's 3 Years in a Well
cases.cause: Three years earlier the King of Wuji bound an incarnation of Manjushri (as a monk) and soaked him in the imperial river for three days
cases.effect: Manjushri's mount, the green-maned lion, pushed the king into the Eight-Treasure Glass Well, where he wrongfully died for three years
cases.karma_principle: You soaked me three days, I push you three years — wrongful retribution repaid in kind

cases.cause: Burned Wukong with Samadhi true fire, harmed countless lives, and wanted to eat Tang Sanzang
cases.effect: Guanyin subdued him with a lotus platform formed from heavenly blades, taking him as the Wealth-Bestowing Boy, never again entering samsara
cases.karma_principle: Evil karma can be transformed by higher karma; recruitment is 'evil karma turned to good fruit'

cases.case_name: Wukong's Havoc and 500 Years under a Mountain
cases.cause: Wreaked havoc in the Heavenly Palace, stole peaches and elixirs, disrupted the Peach Banquet, and made himself the Heavenly Court's enemy
cases.effect: The Tathāgata pressed him under Five Elements Mountain for 500 years, eating iron pellets when hungry and drinking molten copper when thirsty
cases.karma_principle: Great evil requires great atonement; 500 years repaid it, and after atonement he attained the true fruit

cases.cause: Golden Cicada slighted the Dharma and was demoted to the mortal world by the Tathāgata
cases.effect: His first 9 lives as a monk were all devoured by Sha Wujing at the Flowing Sands River, their skulls hung on Wujing's neck; in the 10th life Xuanzang completed the pilgrimage
cases.karma_principle: Past-life karma is repaid in this life; 9 lives of hardship prepared the 10th life's Buddhahood

cases.cause: Drunk at the Peach Banquet, flirted with Chang'e; with lust rising, he knocked over the Dipper-and-Ox Palace
cases.effect: The Jade Emperor demoted him to the mortal world, where he was wrongly cast into a sow's womb, became ugly, and turned demon at Cloud-Tunnel Cave on Mount Fuling
cases.karma_principle: Lust breeds retribution for lust; wrongly cast into the animal realm, he attained the true fruit after atonement

cases.case_name: Sha Wujing's Shattered Goblet and Demotion
cases.cause: Accidentally shattered a glass goblet at the Peach Banquet — a breach of ritual
cases.effect: The Jade Emperor demoted him to the mortal world, where a flying sword pierced his chest every seven days; he became an ogre at the Flowing Sands River and ate passing travelers
cases.karma_principle: The Heavenly Court's rites are strict; even an accident is heavily punished, yet after atonement he attained the true fruit

cases.cause: Kui Mulang eloped with the Jade Maiden of the Incense Hall, and both descended to the world as demons
cases.effect: Kui Mulang was demoted to the world as the Yellow-Robed Demon, had a 13-year marriage with Princess Baihuaxiu, and ate people and did evil
cases.karma_principle: The karma of adultery attracted a 13-year predestined marriage; once the retribution ended, each returned to their proper place

cases.case_name: The Womanland Marriage That Never Was
cases.cause: Tang Sanzang and the Queen of Womanland had unfinished karmic bonds, but a tribulation test lay ahead, so marriage was impossible
cases.effect: Tang Sanzang feigned marriage to obtain the passport; a scorpion spirit abducted him, and the Queen of Womanland was left alone in her chamber
cases.karma_principle: The pilgrim faces a love trial, but fixed karma takes priority; the tribulation cannot be avoided, only refused

cases.cause: Family troubles with Rākṣasī, defeat in magical combat with Wukong, encirclement by the gods, and desperation on all sides
cases.effect: The Bull Demon King revealed his true form as a great white bull, was subdued by Nezha, and submitted to the Heavenly Court and Vulture Peak
cases.rebirth_destination: Submitted as an orthodox deity's retinue
cases.karma_principle: Those with deep evil karma are subdued by force and reformed; not voluntary, but ultimately good fruit

karma_stats.common_pattern: 7 of the 10 cases ultimately 'attain the true fruit or reform' — showing the Journey to the West view of karma is 'transformable,' not fixed
karma_stats.karma_balance: Evil karma can be transformed through 'atonement, recruitment, and forcible reform,' but fixed karma (such as the Womanland love trial) cannot be changed

karma_insights: The Journey to the West view of karma is 'transformable,' not 'fixed'; 7 of 10 cases ultimately attain the true fruit
Karma outweighs Heaven's decree; though the Jing River Dragon King defied the Jade Emperor, his execution was karma's due
Karma outweighs the registers; the register can be changed but karma cannot be escaped — Tang Sanzang still had to repay karma across 9 lives
Wrongful retribution is repaid in kind; the King of Wuji soaked a monk 3 days and was pushed into a well 3 years — a 1:365 ratio
Retribution for lust is heaviest; Bajie's flirtation with Chang'e cast him into the animal realm — lust breeding retribution for lust
Even negligence is heavily punished; Sha Wujing's shattered goblet demoted him — showing the Heavenly Court's rites are strict
Tribulations cannot be changed but can be avoided; the Womanland marriage was a tribulation test, not fixed karma
